newsitem.title: CANADA: United Grain to use new shares to pay debt.
newsitem.headline: United Grain to use new shares to pay debt.

text.p: A new issue last week of two million United Grain Growers Ltd shares will be used to repay bank debts, UGG's chief executive Brian Hayward told shareholders at the firm's annual meeting.

"Last week, market conditions presented UGG with the opportunity to issue additional equity at C$11 per share. That money, in the very short run, will be used to pay down bank indebtedness," Hayward said.
UGG held 17 percent of the share of Canada's grain handling market in fiscal year 1996 (Aug/July).
UGG and Saskatchewan Wheat Pool are the only two publicly traded Canadian grain handlers.
"We will, in time, use the proceeds to continue our ongoing program of facilities modernization," Hayward added.

UGG trimmed its network of primary elevators across Canada's Prairies to 173 by July 31, 1996, down 21 percent from 220 facilities a year earlier, while building massive high throughput elevators in their place.
Bank of Nova Scotia unit Scotia McLeod and Bank of Montreal unit Nesbitt Burns underwrote last week's share offer.
An option to buy 500,000 more shares has not yet been exercised, a Scotia McLeod official said.

"If you can replace debt with equity, that's a smart move," said Scotia McLeod vice-president Fred Ketchen. "It seems to me that UGG has an interesting future ahead of it. World population is rising, cultivated area is dropping per capita and slowly economic conditions continue to improve and what happens is consumption of meat rises which means more demand for grain."
UGG posted positive earnings per share of C$0.45 in fiscal 1996 compared to a net loss of C$0.84 a share in the previous year.

"As a company, we are aware of the fact that our results are inadequate. They are much improved this year. Our objective is to produce as good, if not better results. That's why we're investing in at a higher rate than any of the other grain handlers," UGG chief financial officer Peter Cox told shareholders.
UGG shares traded at C$10.95 each on the Toronto Stock Exchange at 1240 EST. Volume was 1,008.
"UGG's shares are thinly traded. One impact is that there can be days when the price moves around on very low volume," UGG's Hayward said.

"Another impact, with a relatively small market capitalization by Toronto standards, is that when there is buying interest there can be difficulty for investors to take a position," he said of the decision to issue new shares.
The new issue was expected to change UGG's working capital ratio to 1.39 from 1.28 and bring the absolute level of working capital to C$92.5 million, he said.
Debt-to-assets should decline to 46 percent from 52 percent if the new shares generate C$21 million, Hayward said.
